description: ol-undefined-var (issue #1102): a `local` initializer is evaluated BEFORE the new binding is created, "with exactly the visibility the `local` statement itself has — the current scope minus any new binding the declaration creates" (spec/execution-model.md:508-515). With no other visible `x`, `local x = :x` therefore reads a name nothing has bound yet. Until issue #825 replaced this rule's order-free per-frame set with a per-statement scope model, `x` was a lexical member of the frame and the read checked clean. The conforming snapshot idiom the same spec text exists to allow — `local x = 1` then `local x = :x`, where the second initializer reads the FIRST binding — stays clean, and is pinned in packages/parser/src/variable-visibility.test.mjs alongside the parameter and `global` cases; a fix that excluded the declared name unconditionally would satisfy this fixture and reject that conforming program.
